fun_highlights: The dynasty layer has genuine mechanical depth: seat progression (0-7), reputation tags that accumulate and fade, heirlooms that create latent memories in heirs, a family secret that propagates, and the motto crystallization. These are real long-game levers, not cosmetic.

The bequest choice (mind/means/heart/free) is a satisfying cross-generational player lever — a deliberate decision that visibly shapes the next life's starting conditions. It creates a feeling of authorship across generations.

Seat-gated and repute-gated cards (s_great_burden, s_patronage, r_scholar_door, r_family_shadow, the hard-name deal closer) mean high-standing dynasties genuinely encounter content that low-standing lines never see. A family risen to a grand estate plays a structurally different game.

The m_invest_name card gives the dynasty-minded player a direct spend-yourself-to-lift-the-house lever. Combined with the reckoning card, there is a real economy of dynasty management — not just witnessing, but steering.

Callback cards (cb_books_late, cb_lookaway, cb_outcast_return, cb_strayed, cb_inherited_secret) are the game's best feature: they make earlier choices feel consequential later, and the inherited_secret chain across generations is the most interesting narrative thread in the whole system.
The epitaph anti-repetition logic (cluster blocking across 2 ancestors) is well-designed and visible in the transcripts — the chronicle actually reads differently house to house.
The 91-card pool is large enough that individual lives rarely feel identical; the diversity of choices encountered per life is real.
staleness: The life-shape template is highly consistent across all 38 lives: childhood fever + friend/book/animal → mentor at 14-21 → fall-in-love → marry late → one child at 40+ → body warning at 60 → legacy question at 75 → death. Across 12 dynasties, this arc becomes familiar enough that by dynasty 5 or 6 the reader is anticipating beats, not discovering them.

The 'Was taken under a wing' (y_mentor) card fires in 13 of 38 lives — nearly every other life. The 'Began from nothing' (s_from_nothing) card fires 7 times, meaning every dynasty of low standing resets to the same foundational card. These high-frequency anchors make the early adult phase feel like a template.

Child marriage is consistently late (age 40-55) across almost all lives regardless of character — a mechanical consequence of card pacing (love at 16-25, marry at 24-58 gated on love, child gated on marriage) that makes every generation's arc emotionally similar even when names change.

The dynasty layer rarely generates genuinely divergent narrative tension. The reckoning card (x_reckoning) fired once in 38 lives and 12 dynasties. The inheritance dispute (s_inheritance_dispute) and s_patronage cards were invisible. The seat-gated variety is almost entirely absent from the transcript record because most dynasties stay at seat 0-3 and never trigger it.

The motto system converges on a narrow set: 'What the mind holds cannot be taken' and 'We burn bright, and we burn' account for 4 of 7 mottos earned. The reputation pathways that lead to scholarly and reckless are over-represented relative to pious, artistic, generous. Players steering for variety still land in the same two houses.

Cross-generational continuity is thin as active memory rather than as implicit flavour. The heirlooms feel meaningful in prose but only the 'book' and 'stray' heirlooms generate callback cards that visibly fire. A 'name that opens doors by being feared' heirloom appears in many lineages but rarely produces a seat-gated moment — the hard-name deal card fired twice, both in the same dynasty. The felt impact of a fearsome or learned name on the moment-to-moment gameplay is low for most houses.

Generational variety is more about prose flavour than structural divergence. Dynasty 1 (scholarly) and Dynasty 12 (reckless-motto, generous) look different in their final epitaphs, but the sequence of moments encountered is more similar than different — both include the fever, the mentor, the love, the book, the late marriage, the health scare, the legacy question. The variation is in which branch was taken, not in what was presented.

The 'one more dynasty' pull is weak because there is no explicit goal structure or dynasty challenge to complete. A player who has steered one scholarly house and one reckless house has essentially seen the system's range. There is no antagonist, no surprise reversal mechanic, no 'has this ever happened before' moment generated by the dynasty systems colliding.

improvements.what: Increase the reckoning and inheritance-dispute fire rate, and add 1-2 more external-pressure cards (a rival house making a move, a political upheaval that costs a seat) that gate on seat >= 3.
improvements.why: The current dynasty loop is entirely internal: you build, the house rises. There is no adversarial pressure, no risk of being overtaken or destabilised from outside. The reckoning is the only external shock and it fires once in 38 lives. Adding threatened-seat moments would make the long game feel like a campaign rather than a growth chart.

improvements.what: Add 2-3 dynasty-specific cards that only appear ONCE PER DYNASTY (not once per life), tied to milestones: first time the house reaches seat 4, first motto earned, first time a life dies before having children.
improvements.why: Right now every individual card is gated per-life. Dynasty milestones (reaching a grand estate, earning the words) generate a log line, but no decision card. A dynasty-milestone card would make the long-game player feel the house as a character with its own beats, not just a stat bar.

improvements.what: Add 3-4 reputation-specific callback cards beyond the existing r_scholar_door and r_family_shadow. A 'reckless house' should get a youth card where the heir rides the family legend; a 'generous house' should get a card where someone presumes on the open door; a 'kind house' should get a card where the reputation is tested by someone undeserving.
improvements.why: The repute system accumulates for 3-7 generations but only materialises in gameplay via two cards (the scholar door and the shadow). Making every reputation path feel like a different flavour of life would make the dynasty choice feel like choosing a genre, not just a label.

improvements.what: Reduce the frequency of y_mentor (currently fires in ~34% of all lives) by raising the minimum cooldown or adding a gating condition so it cannot fire in consecutive generations of the same dynasty.
improvements.why: The single most repeated card pattern across the transcripts is: childhood → mentor at 14-21. This card is doing so much weight-lifting (mind boost, relationship, teaching heirloom) that removing or throttling it would make both the teaching heirloom and the 'self-made' branch feel more significant.

improvements.what: Add one 'twist on the template' card per stage that inverts the normal narrative — a late-life first love that breaks up a long marriage, a youth mentor who turns out to have taken something from the character, a midlife windfall that comes with a moral cost attached.
improvements.why: The existing cards are almost uniformly structured as 'net positive' vs 'net negative' choices with clear framing. A card that starts as one thing and reveals itself as another would create the 'emergent story' moment the game currently lacks — the moment where the simulation surprises you.

improvements.what: Give the player a dynasty chronicle view (accessible in-game, not just post-session) that names the house's current reputation trajectory and explicitly shows what the next milestone is — how far from the next seat, how close to a motto, whether the secret is still buried.
improvements.why: The dynasty layer has real mechanical depth but it is mostly invisible mid-play. Players who enjoy building a house can only infer what they are building. Making the scoreboard legible would create explicit goals that sustain the 'one more generation' pull.

verdict: The dynasty layer has the architecture for a genuinely engaging long game — seat progression, reputation accumulation, heirlooms, secrets, seat-gated content — but in practice the same life template (fever, mentor, late love, late child, health scare, legacy question) recurs across nearly every life, the reckoning and high-standing cards almost never fire, and by dynasty 5 or 6 you are watching variation on a template rather than discovering new structure.
